source_title: India INDIA Bloc Postpones 'Public Impeachment' Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar To Oct 31
source_excerpt:
The INDIA bloc's proposed “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar has been postponed to October 31, sources said.
The event, which was scheduled to be held on Friday, is being organised by opposition parties as a symbolic protest against Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for his resignation.
According to the sources, the programme has been postponed due to incessant rain in the national capital.
INDIA bloc leaders finalised the decision to hold the programme at a meeting on Thursday. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar was scheduled to chair the proceedings, while Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge was to move a symbolic motion. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was expected to deliver the concluding remarks.
The programme was planned for 3:30 pm at Kharge's residence at 10 Rajaji Marg. Opposition leaders, including Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Jairam Ramesh and K C Venugopal, along with TMC's Derek O'Brien, Samajwadi Party's Harendra Malik, JMM's Mahua Maji and CPI(M)'s John Brittas, were among those who attended the meeting to finalise the event.
According to PTI, one representative from each INDIA bloc party was likely to speak at the programme, with invitations sent to MPs.

The INDIA bloc has accused Kumar of violating constitutional principles and undermining the electoral process. The opposition has been demanding his resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.
After the meeting on Thursday, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that the CEC had violated the Constitution and misled the Supreme Court.
“The CEC has demonstrably violated the letter and spirit of the Constitution. He has systematically subverted the very foundations of our electoral democracy. He has, to put it bluntly, lied to the Supreme Court,” Ramesh had said.
He further alleged that Kumar had acted on behalf of the ruling establishment, saying, “He has been the willing executioner on behalf of the Diabolical Duo whose turn will come next.”
The Congress had also claimed on Tuesday that it was denied permission to hold the event, accusing the government of attempting to silence ordinary citizens after, according to the party, undermining the electoral system.
The proposed “public impeachment” is a symbolic political protest by the opposition and not a formal constitutional impeachment proceeding.
The event, originally scheduled for Friday, has been postponed to October 31. This decision was reported by news agency PTI, citing sources.

He holds a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Lucknow and a Postgraduate Diploma in Public Administration. He was elected National Treasurer of the Press Club of India. His reporting portfolio spans political developments as well as parliamentary affairs.
Over the course of his career, he has extensively covered several major electoral events, including the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections of 2007, 2013, 2017 and 2022, along with the Lok Sabha elections of 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He has also reported from the ground during Assembly elections in multiple states across the country.
Among his notable assignments are exclusive field reports from the 2013 Uttarakhand floods, coverage of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s transition from Gujarat to Delhi, and continuous reporting throughout the Covid-19 pandemic. He also provided comprehensive coverage of Rahul Gandhi’s Bharat Jodo Yatra and Nyay Yatra.
